main_text.p: للللرجال مكرمة للنسا Circumcisio ritus est Viris [necessarius] in fœminis honorabilis: cui addi potest quod ab eodem refert Ebnol Athir, في الوليمة الاعذار حق Æquum est ut circumcisiones convivio celebrentur. Quod ad ipsum Mohammedem, eum natum asserunt معذورا مسرورا Umbilico, & præputio, præcisis. quod si fictum, ideò factum videtur,ut Mosi, vel alicui alii è Patriarchis, de quibus idem asserunt Iudæi, similis haberetur; sin verum, non adeò insolens fuisse, ut pueri recutiti nascerentur,apud gentes circumcisionis observantes, patet ex iis quæ statuunt Iudæi in suis ad legem [illegible, ~10 letters] de iis, qui hoc modo ex utero materno prodierint. Nisi forsan verpum hunc sub Lunæ radiis natum putemus. Credebant siquidem Arabes ان من ولد في القمر
מהורל[?]Illi qui sub Luna radiis nascerētur contrahi perinde ac circumcisio praeputium, teste Authore libri Rambam tract. de circumcis. c. 1. تراجعت قلفته فكان كالمغتون ذظم الدر[?]

Sanguis ] Videntur tamen Arabes antiquiores sanguinem inter esculenta habuisse, unde inter ea, quæ iis olim in usu erant, numeratur التسويں seu intestina sanguine ad escam farciendi mos, apud authorem libri Nosthroldorr, كانوا يجعلون الدم في الامعاء ويلقو ذه في النار ثم يأكلونه Sanguinem intestinis inditum, atque in ignem conjectum comedebant. Cibum istum مسون[?] Atoswadd, ab اسود quod nigrum denotat, appellabant, ut nostrates Black pudding. Et v. AlZamachilh, & Bidawium. in c. 5. Alc. ubi probibetur sanguis. Ira autem conficiebatur ان يوخذ الدمران فتعصر فيها الناقة ويشن راسها وذشري ويوكل describente.

page.notes: Marginal notes: left margin, top: "AlGazal. & v. Mogreb. in" with an Arabic word below; left margin, middle: "Ebnol Athir. ibid."; left margin, bottom: Hebrew "קטן שנולד" and "בשהוא[?]", the last word only partly legible. The Greek word after "ad legem" is too blurred to read and is marked illegible. The Arabic passages are copied as seen and may contain small errors; the Arabic in the first line is partly obscured. The printed text is set in the same paragraph throughout, with no paragraph break on this part of the page. The first line of the Latin in the margin and the Hebrew heading are uncertain. The Arabic lines are read only roughly, and the Arabic word after "libri" and the word "Atoswadd" are doubtful. The blot in the left-margin note after "sanguis" hides part of the word. The word "describente" is split across two lines in the print.
